name: Liu Song
info: The first of the four Southern dynasties of China, founded by the general Liu Yu at Jiankang, remembered for the prosperous Reign of Yuanjia, its wars with Northern Wei and its violent court.
t: Liu Yu, a general of the Jin who had retaken Chang'an and Luoyang, received the abdication of Sima Dewen in 420 and founded the Song dynasty.
The Reign of Yuanjia (425–453) under Emperor Wen is remembered as one of the relative golden ages of the Southern Dynasties.
Failed wars against Northern Wei and murderous succession struggles weakened the dynasty until Xiao Daocheng took the throne as Emperor of Qi in 479.
dyk: The astronomer Zu Chongzhi, who lived in the Liu Song period, is noted for calculating pi to seven decimal places.
ev: Liu Yu captures the Southern Yan capital at Guanggu, ending Southern Yan
Sima Dewen abdicates in favour of Liu Yu, who founds the Song dynasty
The Reign of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen brings prosperity and stable administration
Emperor Wen's great invasion of Northern Wei ends in disaster, and the provinces south of the Yellow River are laid waste
The heir apparent Liu Shao assassinates Emperor Wen and is overthrown by his brother Liu Jun, Emperor Xiaowu
Liu Ziye succeeds his father and rules as a tyrant until his uncle assassinates him
Xiao Daocheng takes the throne as Emperor of Qi, ending the Liu Song

sections.foundation:
Liu Yu was born in poverty and joined the army young. In 399 he fought against the Five Pecks of Rice rebellion led by Sun Tai and Sun En, and in 404 he was instrumental in defeating the usurpation of the general Huan Xuan, after which he was given command of the Beifu corps. Leading the Jin armies, he captured the Southern Yan capital at Guanggu by the spring of 410, retook Chengdu and the land of Shu by advancing along the Min River, and, after the death of the Later Qin emperor Yao Xin, defeated Later Qin and a Northern Wei army and recaptured Chang'an and Luoyang.

After Liu Mengzhi died, Liu Yu returned to Jiankang to secure his power, and the state of Xia reoccupied Guanzhong. In 419 he had Emperor An of Jin strangled and replaced by his brother Sima Dewen, posthumously Emperor Gong, who abdicated in his favour in 420. The new dynasty took its name from Liu's fief, roughly the territory of the Spring and Autumn era State of Song. Liu did not present his regime as a restoration of the Han, though related to the Han imperial family. He died in 422.
sections.socioeconomy:
Under Emperor Wen the Liu Song economy prospered during the Reign of Yuanjia, from 425 to 453, a period noted for its prosperity within the four hundred years of conflict between the Han and Tang dynasties. It is remembered for political stability and capable administration, credited both to the emperor and to his strong and honest officials.

That prosperity was damaged by war. After the failed invasion of Northern Wei in 450, the provinces south of the Yellow River were devastated. Sima Guang describes the Wei forces laying South Yan, Xu, North Yan, Yu, Qing and Ji Provinces to waste: young men beheaded or cut in half, infants killed on spears, commanderies and counties burned and slaughtered until not even grass was left. The economic damage was immense. Later, under Emperor Ming, the surrender of the northern commanderies to Wei cost the dynasty its most fertile and cultivated lands.
sections.military:
Liu Yu is regarded as one of the best generals of the Northern and Southern dynasties. At one battle against Northern Wei he is recorded as using spears launched by crossbows, which panicked the Wei cavalry and gave him a decisive victory. His successors were less able. In 422, the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, three commanderies were lost to Wei, though the general Dao Yanzhi later recovered Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao south of the Yellow River. Wen's refusal to advance further let Wei destroy the ally Xia and unify the north in 439.

Wen executed the general Tan Daoji and took command himself. In 450 he launched a massive invasion of Northern Wei; the Wei lured his armies across the Yellow River, flanked them and destroyed the Eastern army, and only the fortified city of Huatai held out. Sima Guang blamed the emperor's insistence that generals follow his own plans and the untrained conscripts. A second attempt in 452 also failed. In the civil war against his nephew Liu Zixun, Emperor Ming's generals captured Kuaiji and Qianxi and starved the rebel army into collapse.
sections.governance:
The Liu Song was ruled by emperors of the Liu family from Jiankang. Its history was one of internal turmoil, with several rulers judged incompetent or tyrannical and met with military revolts. After the founder's death in 422 his successor Shaodi was quickly removed, and the throne passed to his third son, Emperor Wen. Wen's reign was stable, but in 453 his heir apparent, Liu Shao, assassinated him, an act seen as a breach of the Confucian principle of filial piety. Liu Jun rose against him, beheaded him and became Emperor Xiaowu.

Xiaowu's son Liu Ziye, who succeeded in 464, is generally regarded as a tyrant who put several of his uncles to death; one of those uncles assassinated him and became Emperor Ming. Ming ordered his predecessor's brother and sister to commit suicide, defeated his nephew Liu Zixun, and executed thousands of members of the royal family, so that at his death his son needed the general Xiao Daocheng to govern. In 440 the dynasty changed its official religion to Taoism, replacing Buddhism.
sections.impact:
The Liu Song produced much poetry, notably the rhapsody, fu. The imperial house sponsored literary works and many of its members wrote themselves; the court of Emperor Wen was especially active and supported the compilation of A New Account of the Tales of the World (Shishuo Xinyu), a large collection of short prose anecdotes. The "Three Giants of Yuanjia", Bao Zhao, Xie Lingyun and Yan Yanzhi, are among the best known poets of the period and are credited as the originators of three major literary trends.

Scientists and astronomers worked in times of relative peace, among them Zu Chongzhi, noted for calculating pi to seven decimal places. Buddhism became better understood and more widely practised, and some officials, such as Xie Lingyun, were Buddhists. Of the Six Dynasties tomb sculptures that survive around Nanjing and Danyang, only one group is securely identified as Liu Song: the two qilin of the Chuning Tomb of the first emperor, in Qilin Town in Nanjing's Jiangning District.
sections.decline:
Emperor Ming's refusal to pardon those who had supported Liu Ziye led the governors of the northern commanderies, fearing execution at Jiankang, to surrender to Wei. The dynasty lost the Chinese heartland and its most fertile lands, and Ming's attempts to recover them were defeated. His purges of his brothers and nephews left the royal family greatly weakened.

His son, Emperor Houfei, resented the control that Xiao Daocheng held over him and said openly several times that he would kill him. Xiao had him assassinated and placed Emperor Shun on the throne. In 479 Xiao took the throne himself as Emperor of Qi, ending the Liu Song, and the former emperor Shun and his clan were soon put to the sword. Some of the family survived in the north: Liu Hui, a descendant of the royal house who fled to Northern Wei, married Princess Lanling, a daughter of Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei.

summary: The Liu Song, founded in 420 by the general Liu Yu after he took the throne of the Eastern Jin, was the first of the Southern dynasties of China. It prospered in the Reign of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen and fostered poetry and science, but defeats by Northern Wei and murderous struggles in the imperial family brought its end in 479.

pointDescs.420: Sima Dewen abdicates and Liu Yu founds the Song, holding the lands won in his campaigns, including Luoyang.
pointDescs.422: Liu Yu dies; three commanderies are lost to Wei in the first year of Emperor Wen.
pointDescs.425: The Reign of Yuanjia begins under Emperor Wen.
pointDescs.439: Northern Wei completes the unification of the north, a lasting threat to the Song.
pointDescs.440: The dynasty changes its official religion to Taoism; the Yuanjia prosperity is at its height.
pointDescs.450: Emperor Wen's invasion of Northern Wei ends in disaster and the provinces south of the Yellow River are devastated.
pointDescs.452: A second attempt to destroy Northern Wei fails.
pointDescs.453: Liu Shao assassinates Emperor Wen and is overthrown by Liu Jun, Emperor Xiaowu, whose reign is relatively peaceful.
pointDescs.464: Liu Ziye succeeds and rules as a tyrant.
pointDescs.466: Emperor Ming defeats Liu Zixun, and the northern commanderies surrender to Wei; the year is placed after Ming's accession, the article giving none.
pointDescs.472: After Emperor Ming's purges his son must be assisted by Xiao Daocheng; the year is approximate, the article giving none.
pointDescs.479: Xiao Daocheng takes the throne as Emperor of Qi, ending the Liu Song.

notes: The article's Sources section is empty, so references are [].
Points 466 and 472 are approximate placements for Liu Zixun's rebellion and Emperor Ming's death; the article dates neither. Editor may prefer to drop them.
The article's phrase 'barbarian' is the article's; I used Northern Wei and Xianbei instead. Liu Zixun 'aged just 10' left out.
The 'Liu Yu' named among tyrants in the lead is Emperor Houfei (also Liu Yu), not the founder; not repeated.
